transcript.text: Zanussi dishwasher keeps tripping the electrics, not every time though. Usually about 15 mins in. Model ZDT21006FA

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. You must not use the appliance until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. The fact that it typically trips around 15 minutes into a cycle suggests an issue with the heating element or its insulation breaking down when hot. Less commonly, it could be the circulation pump or internal wiring. To help the engineer diagnose this more quickly (and to ensure you aren't doing anything unsafe), please confirm: does the trip happen immediately upon switching on, or only after the cycle has started and the water begins to heat? Also, with the machine unplugged, is there any visible moisture or corrosion around the heater element at the bottom of the tub?

It doesn't trip straight away, only about 10-20 mins into the 65C programme. A quick cold rinse has never tripped it. I can't see any moisture or damage, and I'm not taking any covers off to look further. It's on the same circuit as my fridge, which is why I'm a bit worried. No burning smell.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
The fact that it never trips on a cold rinse but consistently trips 10–20 minutes into a hot programme points to an earth fault in the heating element. This is a safety hazard that cannot be fixed by resetting the breaker; it requires a qualified engineer to isolate the appliance, test the element's insulation resistance with specialist equipment, and replace the faulty part (usually the heating element itself).
